s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic vision disturbance with signs of intraocular inflammation and macular edema
salient_findings: Cystoid macular edema with subfoveal fluid
Keratic precipitates and cells in the anterior chamber
key_facts: 65-year-old woman
Blurry vision in right eye for several months
History of 3 episodes of bilateral iritis
Amblyopia in left eye
Bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens
Left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior
On anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years
Visual acuity 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS
Normal intraocular pressures
Conjunctival injection and fine keratic precipitates in right eye
Cystoid macular edema with yellow spot in fovea in right eye
Epiretinal membrane in left eye
Normal blood tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders
Unremarkable computed tomography of the chest

shortlist.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic intraocular inflammation and history of bilateral iritis

shortlist.label: Ankylosing spondylitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurrent bilateral iritis and signs of intraocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic vision disturbance and signs of intraocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Birdshot chorioretinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic intraocular inflammation and macular edema

shortlist.label: Seronegative spondyloarthropathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurrent bilateral iritis and signs of intraocular inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's history of recurrent bilateral iritis and the presence of cystoid macular edema are consistent with seronegative spondyloarthropathy, which is known to cause uveitis and other ocular manifestations.

rejected.label: Fuchs heterochromic iridocyclitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with heterochromia of the iris, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Ankylosing spondylitis
rejected.why: No mention of systemic symptoms such as back pain or stiffness, which are common in ankylosing spondylitis

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Normal blood tests and unremarkable computed tomography of the chest make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Birdshot chorioretinopathy
rejected.why: Typically presents with distinctive birdshot lesions in the retina, which are not mentioned in the case
